claims.statement: For the stated S->2S, S->0, S->R, S->U branching model with fixed a,q and common b-d, the full expected-count trajectories (E[S_t], E[R_t], E[U_t]) are identical for all (b,d) pairs with the same net birth rate b-d.
assumptions: constant rates during the fixed action
R and U persistent nonbranching marks
claims.novelty_boundary: The mean matrix depending on division/death through net rate is explicit in Gunnarsson-Foo-Leder; no novelty is claimed. This does not conflict with identification of constant two-state CTMC rates from a nonconstant full trajectory.
costs: Exact expected curves require no data cost but do not encode the clone-level distribution.
claims.falsifier: Under the assumed generator, directly derived state-count means fail to satisfy the displayed linear ODE or differ between parameter pairs with the same b-d and same action rates.
claims.next_gate: Check the branching and persistent-mark assumptions in a specified experimental context.

claims.statement: At T=1, worlds (b,d)=(1,0.5) and (10.5,10), with action A=(a,q)=(0.1,0) and action B=(0.2,0.3), have equal expected S/R/U curves arm-by-arm but reverse the ranking of J=P(R_T>0,U_T=0): B>A in the first world and A>B in the second.
assumptions: J is founder-level target success without any U mark at T
claims.proof_path: PGF derivation in CYCLE2_REPORT.md; exact Riccati values and independent RK4 checks in branching_safety_controller.py and branching_safety_controller_results.json
claims.novelty_boundary: The branching PGF and net-growth alias are standard; this is a scoped decision-reversal witness, not a priority claim. Stronger lineage/count-distribution methods can distinguish the worlds.
costs: Model calculations only; no experimental data acquired.
claims.falsifier: Substitution into the PGF ODE or an independent exact solver changes either success probability enough to remove the strict opposite rankings.
claims.next_gate: Compare founder-level safety decisions against the full Gunnarsson likelihood and Ventre lineage baseline on equal independent founders and assay burden.

claims.statement: For the stated model and exact unconditional terminal clone moments mS=E[S_T], mR=E[R_T], mU=E[U_T], and vS=Var(S_T), one terminal census identifies b,d,a,q through the inversion in CYCLE2_REPORT.md, including the r=0 limit.
assumptions: complete clone recovery with original founder roster, including extinct clones as zero
constant rates and persistent nonbranching R/U marks
claims.proof_path: Moment derivation and inverse in CYCLE2_REPORT.md; reconstructed rates in branching_safety_controller_results.json
claims.novelty_boundary: Gunnarsson-Foo-Leder already use count variation/covariance to separate division/death after net and switching rates; this report claims only a one-terminal-moment sufficient statistic for this restricted model, not a new general estimator or assay-minimality theorem.
costs: One terminal timepoint; complete per-founder counts/state labels; independent founder replication to estimate moments. No finite-sample rate confidence bound is claimed from the algebra alone.
claims.falsifier: A symbolic or exact moment calculation under the stated branching law fails to recover its rates, or a nondegenerate model parameter pair produces the same four moments but different rates.
claims.next_gate: Build finite-sample confidence sets for these moments under realistic lineage dropout, overdispersion, and donor clustering.

claims.statement: For m independently randomized fixed actions with n independent founder clones per action and perfectly classified binary target/harm outcomes, the rule using h=sqrt(log(4m/alpha)/(2n)), UCB(harm)<=delta, and maximal LCB(target) has simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha; every selected action obeys the risk cap on that event, and has target regret at most 2h versus any action with risk at most delta-2h.
assumptions: binary endpoints are fixed before randomization
action costs known or separately bounded
claims.proof_path: Algorithm and union-bound derivation in CYCLE2_REPORT.md; sample arithmetic in branching_safety_controller.py and branching_safety_controller_results.json
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a standard finite-sample safe best-arm rule applied to founder-level clone outcomes; no algorithmic novelty is claimed.
costs: For m=2, alpha=0.05, and half-width 0.05, 1,016 independent founders per arm; all descendant reads, calibration, culture, and biological replicate costs are additional.
claims.falsifier: The coverage or regret statement fails under the stated independent Bernoulli outcome contract.
claims.next_gate: Replace perfect classification with calibrated sensitivity/specificity and donor-level randomization; preregister risk margin and validation cohort.

claims.statement: With J cause-specific counting processes, predictable exposure Aj<=Amax, hazard lambda_j<=Lambda, and a unit-jump event-count martingale, beta=sqrt(2 Lambda Amax log(2J/alpha))+(2/3)log(2J/alpha) gives simultaneous |Cj-lambda_j Aj|<=beta with probability at least 1-alpha.
claims.proof_path: Counting-process confidence-set section in CYCLE2_REPORT.md; radius computation in branching_safety_controller.py and branching_safety_controller_results.json
claims.novelty_boundary: Freedman/Bernstein concentration is standard. This is included to expose rate-acquisition costs; it is not required for direct founder-outcome safety selection.
costs: Illustrative Lambda=12, Amax=200, J=6, alpha=0.05 gives a 165.85-event radius, too broad for useful rate separation.
claims.falsifier: The stated counting process violates its intensity/cap assumptions or the asserted martingale tail event exceeds alpha.
claims.next_gate: Set exposure budgets from a real platform pilot; otherwise return UNKNOWN.

primary_sources_reviewed.title: Statistical inference of the rates of cell proliferation and phenotypic switching in cancer
primary_sources_reviewed.scope_reconstructed: Multitype branching model; mean matrix depends on b,d through net b-d; pure-start derivatives identify switching/net rates; covariance information can identify birth rates; likelihood-based estimation and confidence intervals.

primary_sources_reviewed.title: Trajectory inference for a branching SDE model of cell differentiation via lineage tracing
primary_sources_reviewed.scope_reconstructed: Generation-number reweighting has an asymptotic trajectory guarantee with no death and all leaves observed; death/subsampling creates explicitly analyzed bias.

primary_sources_reviewed.title: Inferring Cell-State Transition Dynamics from Lineage Trees and Endpoint Single-Cell Measurements
primary_sources_reviewed.scope_reconstructed: Lineage-tree kin correlations and endpoint gene-expression measurements for transition inference.

primary_sources_reviewed.title: Transcompp: understanding phenotypic plasticity by estimating Markov transition rates for cell state transitions
primary_sources_reviewed.scope_reconstructed: Time-series composition fitting with optional relative state-specific proliferation estimates.
